editorial.headline: Navigation Safety Systems: Open Nationally, Registrable in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Installation and maintenance of navigation-support systems is open to full foreign ownership nationally and is not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
At its core, this activity is about installing and maintaining the systems and equipment that make sea, river and air navigation safer. The scope includes related equipment for navigation aids; telecommunications serving shipping and aviation; hydrography and meteorology; transit channels; and pilotage. It is a connected technical field: each of those elements is named as serving the safety of shipping and aviation. The work is not limited to first installation. Maintenance belongs to the activity as well, making the scope as much about keeping critical navigation-support systems in working order as putting them in place. The record also identifies construction-installation subclassification IN005.

Registration is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar business scales. This is not a narrow scale category reserved to one class of enterprise; all four scale categories appear explicitly in the record. The defining question is the nature of the work, rather than whether the applicant sits at the smaller or larger end of that stated range. Its boundary is technical and functional: installation or upkeep must concern the named navigation, telecommunications, hydrographic, meteorological, channel or pilotage systems and equipment, with shipping and aviation safety as the stated purpose.

Nationally, the PMA position is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain terms, the record permits full foreign ownership at the national level: there is no foreign-stake cap below 100% stated for this activity. That is the national answer, and it should not be diluted by assumptions about the location of the work or the apparent technical specificity of the systems involved. The ownership ceiling is explicit rather than inferred. The cited national PMA source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali requires a separate reading, but on this record it does not reverse the national position. The Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the activity is not blocked by the provincial PMA moratorium. At the Besar scale, OSS assigns the activity Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi risk. The Bali rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, permanently. The higher risk assessment given here is the reason recorded for the activity falling outside that moratorium. For a foreign investor, the conclusion is direct: this activity can be registered in Bali today, with national foreign ownership available up to 100%.
